Agent Harness Capabilities

The Deep Agents harness provides a robust runtime environment with built-in capabilities.

File System Access

The harness automatically provides standard file system tools to the agent, allowing it to interact with the configured backend.

  • ls: List files in the current directory.
  • read_file: Read the contents of a file.
  • write_file: Write content to a new or existing file.
  • edit_file: specific line-based edits to a file.
  • glob: Find files matching a pattern (e.g., **/*.py).
  • grep: Search for text patterns within files.

Large Tool Result Eviction

To prevent context window overflows, the harness uses FilesystemMiddleware to monitor tool outputs.

  • Threshold: Defaults to 20,000 tokens (configurable via tool_token_limit_before_evict).
  • Action: If a tool result exceeds the limit, it is written to the configured backend (filesystem or state).
  • Replacement: The tool result in the conversation history is replaced with a truncated preview and a file reference.
  • Access: The agent can read the full result from the file system if it determines it is necessary.

Pluggable Storage Backends

You can configure where the agent's files and state are stored. See Backends for full details.

  • StateBackend (ephemeral): Files live in the agent's state. Persists within a thread but not across threads when the conversation ends. Useful for temporary working files.
  • FilesystemBackend (local disk): Reads/writes to the actual disk. Useful for local coding assistants.
  • StoreBackend (persistent): Uses LangGraph's BaseStore. Files persist across conversations and threads. Useful for long-term memory.
  • CompositeBackend: Routes paths to different backends (e.g., /memories/ to StoreBackend, / to StateBackend).

Task Delegation (Subagents)

The harness supports hierarchical task execution via subagents. See Subagents for details.

  • Context Isolation: Subagent work doesn't clutter the main agent's context.
  • Parallelism: Multiple subagents can run concurrently.
  • Specialization: Subagents can have their own tools and prompts.
  • Usage: The main agent uses the task tool to delegate work.

Conversation History Summarization

The harness automatically manages long conversations to stay within the model's context window.

  • Trigger: Activates when the conversation history reaches 85% of the model's max_input_tokens (defined in the model profile).
  • Retention: Keeps the most recent 10% of tokens as immediate context.
  • Summarization: Older messages are compressed into a summary which is inserted as a system message.
  • Transparent: This process happens automatically behind the scenes.

Dangling Tool Call Repair

The harness ensures conversation validity even when interruptions occur.

  • Problem: If a user interrupts the agent or an error occurs after an AIMessage (tool call) but before the ToolMessage (result), the message history becomes invalid.
  • Solution: The harness detects dangling tool calls and inserts synthetic ToolMessages indicating the call was cancelled.
  • Benefit: Prevents "invalid message sequence" errors and allows the agent to resume gracefully.

To-do List Tracking

Enabled by TodoListMiddleware (included by default).

  • Tool: write_todos.
  • Functionality: Allows the agent to track multiple tasks with statuses: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'completed'.
  • Persistence: The list is persisted in the agent's state, helping it stay organized over long horizons.

Human-in-the-loop

Provides safety gates for sensitive operations. See Human-in-the-Loop for configuration.

  • Interrupts: Configure interrupt_on for specific tools (e.g., edit_file).
  • Review: Users can approve, reject, or edit tool calls before they execute.

Prompt Caching (Anthropic)

Automatically enables prompt caching for Anthropic models.

  • Caching: Caches the system prompt and other static prefixes.
  • Benefit: Significantly reduces latency and cost for long system prompts (e.g., those containing large skill documentation).

Streaming

The harness integrates with LangGraph's streaming system to surface updates in real-time.

  • Scope: Streams events from both the main agent and any active subagents.
  • Events: Tool calls, tool results, and LLM tokens are streamed as they occur.
  • Usage: Useful for building UIs that display progress progressively and for debugging agent behavior.
